summary: SEC-002 fixed: logout now revokes the bearer session. Root cause was a missing store.remove() in lib/store.js — the logout handler called it inside an empty catch, so the TypeError was swallowed and the session row survived (live-reproduced: post-logout /api/auth/me returned 200 before the fix, 401 after). Added remove(name,id) to the store (atomic tmp+rename write, returns boolean), rewrote logout() to revoke without swallowing errors (idempotent 200, session_revoked flag), and added 4 regression assertions to apps/lifeboat/test.sh. Full lifeboat suite: 133/133 PASS on fresh ports (129 baseline + 4 new). Multi-session challenge: logging out one token leaves a second session for the same account valid (200), confirming per-session revocation.
root_cause: apps/lifeboat/lib/store.js exported {all,get,insert,update} but no remove(); server.js logout() called store.remove('sessions', token) inside try{}catch{}, so every logout threw TypeError: store.remove is not a function, the catch swallowed it, and the session row was never deleted. Same missing function also silently broke expired-session cleanup in getAuthAccount() (line 210) — fixed as a side effect.

checks.notes: Fresh server on port 18092, fixed code. logout -> {logged_out:true,session_revoked:true}; logged-out token -> 401 on /api/auth/me; second session for same account -> 200 (other sessions/devices unaffected); repeat logout -> 200 (idempotent).
All three files pass syntax check.
RESULT: PASS=133 FAIL=0. Never ran against :8080 demo service (stale pre-fix code); always a fresh port.
Repeat run; SEC-002 assertions individually confirmed: setup token ok; logout 200+session_revoked; logged-out token 401; other session 200. RESULT: PASS=133 FAIL=0.

lessons: An empty catch{} around a call to a non-existent function silently disabled logout for the life of the feature; the same missing store.remove also silently broke expired-session cleanup in getAuthAccount. Prefer explicit boolean results over swallowed exceptions at auth boundaries.

BUG-002 and DAT-001 are absorbed by this fix (same root cause: store.remove missing on logout). DAT-002 (grant sequences spanning multiple non-atomic file writes) is NOT closed by this change — grant atomicity is a separate issue and stays QUEUED.
